title: GLOBAL VIETNAM
sub: In the 1600s, ports in Vietnam drew merchants from across Asia and Europe.
say: In the sixteen hundreds, ports in Vietnam drew merchants from across Asia and Europe.

title: TWO REALMS
sub: In the 1600s, Vietnam was divided. The Nguyễn lords ruled the south, and the Trịnh lords held power in the north. Overseas trade brought the Nguyễn revenue, weapons and information.
say: In the sixteen hundreds, Vietnam was divided. The Nwin lords ruled the south, and the Chin lords held power in the north. Overseas trade brought the Nwin revenue, weapons and information.

title: HỘI AN
sub: In the south, Hội An, known to Europeans as Faifo, became a major port in Asia's sea trade.
say: In the south, Hoy Ahn, known to Europeans as Fy-foh, became a major port in Asia's sea trade.

title: JAPAN TOWN
sub: Japanese merchants arrived on licensed red seal ships, and lived in their own quarter. After Japan banned overseas voyages in 1635, the red seal ships stopped coming, though some Japanese residents stayed on for decades.
say: Japanese merchants arrived on licensed red seal ships, and lived in their own quarter. After Japan banned overseas voyages in sixteen thirty-five, the red seal ships stopped coming, though some Japanese residents stayed on for decades.

title: CHINESE MERCHANTS
sub: Chinese merchants also settled in Hội An. Chinese community halls remain part of the old town today.
say: Chinese merchants also settled in Hoy Ahn. Chinese community halls remain part of the old town today.

title: PHỐ HIẾN
sub: In the north, the Dutch began trading in 1637. Sources differ on whether their station was at Phố Hiến or at the capital. They traded there until 1700, with silk among the main exports.
say: In the north, the Dutch began trading in sixteen thirty-seven. Sources differ on whether their station was at Foh Hee-en or at the capital. They traded there until seventeen hundred, with silk among the main exports.

title: "FIRST THE CAPITAL…"
sub: Phố Hiến itself became a busy river port. A popular saying placed it second: first the capital, second Phố Hiến.
say: Foh Hee-en itself became a busy river port. A popular saying placed it second: first the capital, second Foh Hee-en.

title: DECLINE
sub: Hội An later declined as its harbor silted and other ports, including Đà Nẵng, rose. That stagnation helped preserve the old town. UNESCO listed it in 1999.
say: Hoy Ahn later declined as its harbor silted and other ports, including Dah Nahng, rose. That stagnation helped preserve the old town. UNESCO listed it in nineteen ninety-nine.

title: RICE & EMPIRES
sub: Vietnam's history is not only wars. It is also trade. Follow for more.
say: Vietnam's history is not only wars. It is also trade. Follow for more.
